title: As a marketer, I can compose an email campaign, pick its audience, and send or schedule it — the arena's table-stakes loop
As a developer, I can create and schedule a campaign or broadcast entirely through a documented public API, without touching the dashboard
As an AI-native user, an agent can draft a campaign against a segment and leave it scheduled or queued for a human to approve before send
As a marketer, I can A/B test subject lines or content variants and have the winner picked from real engagement
As a marketer, I can build audience segments from profile attributes, tags, and behavioral events, and they stay live as data changes
As a developer, I can create and update segments, tags, or lists programmatically and read back exactly who is in them
As a developer, I can create, update, and suppress contacts with custom properties through the API at production scale
As an AI-native user, an agent can translate a plain-language audience description into a real segment via the platform's programmatic surface
As a marketer, I can build multi-step lifecycle automations — welcome series, onboarding, winback — with branches, delays, and exit rules
As a developer, I can fire a custom event from my product and have it trigger an automation for exactly that person
As an ops user, I can see where any individual person sits inside an automation and pull or re-enter them without breaking the flow
As a marketer, I can design on-brand emails with a visual editor, reusable templates, and personalization tokens that render correctly across clients
As a developer, I can manage email templates as code — HTML/MJML or API-managed templates with variable substitution — under version control
As a marketer, I can have the platform's built-in AI draft or refine subject lines and email copy from a brief, inside the composer
As an ops user, I can authenticate my own sending domain — SPF, DKIM, DMARC alignment — with guided DNS setup and verification
As an ops user, unsubscribes, bounces, and spam complaints are suppressed automatically and honored across every send type — CAN-SPAM/GDPR hygiene by default
As a marketer, I can see bounce, complaint, and blocklist signals per send and get actionable guidance when deliverability degrades
As a marketer, I can read opens, clicks, unsubscribes, and conversions per campaign and per automation step, over time
As a founder, I can attribute signups or revenue to specific emails and flows, not just opens and clicks
As a developer, I can pull campaign and flow performance metrics through the API into my own warehouse or dashboards
As a developer, I can send one-to-one transactional email — receipts, magic links, notifications — through the same platform's API alongside marketing sends
As an ops user, transactional email is kept separate from marketing — its own templates, suppression rules, and reputation — so a receipt still delivers to an unsubscribed contact
As a founder, I can export my entire audience — contacts, custom fields, tags, engagement history, and suppression list — in an open format, self-serve
As a marketer, I can migrate in from another email platform with guided list import that preserves tags, custom fields, and unsubscribe state
As a developer, I can subscribe webhooks to delivery and engagement events — sends, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes — with a documented, signed payload
As an ops user, I can connect the platform to my existing stack — Stripe or Shopify, a CDP like Segment, my product database — with maintained first-party integrations
As a developer, I can read per-person engagement history — what was sent, opened, clicked — through the API for any contact
As an AI-native user, an agent can pull my whole email program — audiences, live automations, recent campaign results — programmatically and report on what's working
As an ops user, I can mint scoped or read-only API credentials so an agent or contractor can read analytics without the power to send
